title: How a Macaroni Machine Shop Became Curbell Plastics
summary: Curbell Plastics made the 2025 MDM Top Distributors list in Plastics. Its origin story explains why the 80-plus-year-old company still isn't for sale.
body_text: Part of Distributor Playbooks — strategy teardowns of every company on the 2025 MDM Top Distributors lists . Curbell Plastics landed on Modern Distribution Management's 2025 Top Distributors list in the Plastics vertical, one of the largest independent suppliers of plastic sheet, rod, tube, and film in the country. What the ranking doesn't show is where the name came from, or why a company that size has stayed in the same family's hands since Franklin Roosevelt was president. A machine shop on the side of a macaroni plant Curbell's origin has nothing to do with plastic. In the early 1940s, brothers Edmond and Leonard Leone ran a macaroni-producing business in Buffalo, New York, that included, almost incidentally, a small machine shop attached to the operation, according to Curbell's own company history . Buffalo at the time was thick with wartime aviation manufacturing, and the machine shop found its first real customers not in pasta but in airplane parts: Curtiss-Wright and Bell Aircraft, two of the manufacturers building fighters and bombers a few miles from the Leones' plant. The company's name is the tell. "Cur-Bell" is a mashup of Curtiss and Bell, the first two accounts that mattered. It's a small, odd fact, and it explains a lot about how this company thinks: name yourself after the customer, not the product. Plastics came later, as Curbell Medical's history page notes, once the postwar synthetic-materials boom gave a Buffalo machine shop a much bigger material to work with than metal. Two divisions, one family, no obvious reason they belong together Most distributors that reach Curbell's scale pick a lane and go deep. Curbell instead runs two businesses that share a name, a headquarters in Orchard Park, New York, and little else: Curbell Plastics, which sells sheet, rod, tube, film, tape, and fabricated plastic parts to industrial and commercial buyers, and Curbell Medical Products, which makes patient-communication and call-light systems for hospitals. That's an unusual structure to still be running eight decades in. Industrial distribution has spent the last twenty years consolidating under private equity, and the natural move for a family owner sitting on two unrelated divisions would be to sell one, focus the other, and take the multiple. Curbell has done neither. The plastics side has instead used its own balance sheet to keep building itself into, per industry profiles, one of the nation's top-five plastic materials suppliers , while the medical side runs as its own thing entirely. The insight worth naming plainly: staying private and staying diversified across two unrelated verticals is not a placeholder strategy here, it's the strategy, and it's let Curbell make decisions on an eighty-year clock instead of a fund's five-to-seven-year one. Building plastics distribution the boring, compounding way Curbell Plastics itself competes the way specialty material distributors have to: not on price, since sheet and rod are close to commodity inputs, but on the stuff that surrounds the material. The company's site runs an "Ask a Plastics Expert" technical resource, and its sales organization is built around application know-how across markets that each have their own compliance and performance quirks, including oil and gas, aerospace and defense, machine building, transportation, and semiconductors and electronics, per the same industry profile. Add fabrication, cut-to-size processing, and inventory management programs, and the pitch becomes: don't just buy plastic here, offload the plastic problem here. Growth has come from bolting on geography rather than reinventing the model. In its most recent expansion, Curbell Plastics acquired Interstate Advanced Materials , a California-based plastics and composites distributor, adding nine locations to its network in one move. That's the pattern: a company with roughly 18 branches and more than 150 employees a few years ago, according to the same profile, growing largely by buying regional plastics distributors who have the local relationships but not the national purchasing scale, then leaving their people and customer relationships mostly intact. The tension worth sitting with Family ownership at this scale cuts both ways, and Curbell is a useful case study in the trade-off rather than a pure success story. The upside is patience: no earnings call to manage, no private-equity playbook forcing a sale in year five, room to run a medical-device business and a plastics distributor side by side because the owners simply want to. The downside is that the same structure that enabled patience also caps the acquisition firepower available to a distributor competing against PE-backed rivals with committed capital lines built for roll-ups. Curbell has answered that by acquiring carefully rather than constantly, picking targets like Interstate that add geography without adding integration risk. Whether that pace stays sufficient as plastics distribution keeps consolidating is the open question for the next decade, not the last eight. Why it still matters Eighty-plus years after two brothers named a machine shop after their first two aircraft customers, the through-line is consistency of ownership married to steady expansion of reach: more locations, more fabrication capability, more technical depth, same family. In a distribution channel where sheet plastic can look interchangeable branch to branch, Curbell's bet has been that the surrounding service, and the discipline to build it slowly, is the actual product. Every company in this series made the 2025 MDM Top Distributors list for a reason, and underneath most of those rankings sits the same unglamorous machinery: a catalog someone maintains, a branch network someone built, and data that someone has to keep straight for the deal to work at all.

company_name: NCS Multistage Holdings Inc. Common Stock
title: AkerBP North Sea Success Story
body_text: Project description NCS Multistage, together with Aker BP and Alliance partners, has completed a record-setting offshore well in the Valhall field. The completion featured NCS Multicycle™ Frac Sleeves and an NCS Frac-through-coil Isolation Assembly (FIA). The team determined that a conventional frac was not possible due to challenges with the upper completion and decided to stimulate the well using a frac-through-coil approach. A total of nine Shift Frac Close™ stages were completed in fourteen days (including weather delays), with an average proppant placement of 382,000 lbs/stage, setting the following records: New offshore frac-through-coil speed record: 4 stages completed in 34 hours New single stage proppant-through-coil record: 510,000 lbs placed New total proppant-through-coil record: 3,450,000 lbs New total coil length record: 7453 m In total, nearly 3.5M lbs of proppant were successfully placed into nine stages at an average rate of 10.7 bbls/min, with a top proppant concentration of 8 PPA (957 kg/m3). Each frac was underdisplaced to the sand face, followed by cleanout, sleeve closure, and pressure test to confirm successful Shift Frac Close™ completion. The last four stages placed a total of 1.9M lbs of proppant in 34hrs, from the time the sixth MultiCycle™ Frac Sleeve was opened to the time the ninth stage was closed. NCS Multistage, as an Aker BP D&W key strategic partner, aims to surpass these and other records through a collective commitment to continuous improvement.

title: How to Measure DOOH (Digital-Out-of-Home) Campaign Success
summary: Key metrics and effective strategies for analyzing the impact of Digital Out-of-Home advertising The post How to Measure DOOH (Digital-Out-of-Home) Campaign Success appeared first on Perion .
body_text: Key metrics and effective strategies for analyzing the impact of Digital Out-of-Home advertising Measuring the effectiveness of Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) has often been seen as challenging due to its unique parameters and the traditionally based nature of out-of-home advertising. However, with the rise of digital and programmatic technology, marketers now have access to tools and insights that measure Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), using advanced location data and analytics in a similar capacity as other digital channels. Enabled through enhanced data and analytics, marketers can now measure DOOH campaigns based on several KPIs or metrics, including (but not limited to) impressions, audience concentration, footfall traffic to a specific location, offline to online sales, in-store visits, and online engagement or sales lift. Key Highlights: Measuring the performance of OOH campaigns has been a challenge because of the fragmentation of the ecosystem and the traditional nature of the channel. Programmatic technology empowers marketers with tools that use advanced location and audience data and analytics to measure effectiveness and preferred KPIs. Customizable KPIs can measure campaign effectiveness across the entire funnel, from Brand Lift at the top of the funnel to Sales Lift at the bottom. Sales Lift Sales lift studies measure the increase in sales driven by the DOOH campaign exposure against a control number. These studies analyze the effectiveness of advertising by linking consumer exposure to the DOOH ads with subsequent offline sales behavior. By examining the uplift in sales in regions or groups exposed to the campaign versus those not exposed, marketers can directly attribute sales growth to the advertising efforts. This provides a clear view of how DOOH measurements link exposure to offline sales. Sales lift studies also include measuring other metrics, such as sales rate by market, penetration, or dollars per trip. Offline to Online Conversion Unlike traditional OOH, brands launching DOOH campaigns can measure digital KPIs, including: Online Conversions Online sales lift measures the percentage of visitors who complete the desired action online, usually making a purchase, but can also include requesting a demo, completing a form, or downloading a file. It is a key indicator of a campaign’s effectiveness in achieving its goals, and it shows how well it converts traffic into leads or customers online. In-app (IAP) conversions are also a type of online conversion in DOOH since it is connected via a QR code. IAP metrics measure the effectiveness of a monetization strategy within a mobile app. This group of metrics may include conversion rates and average revenue per user (ARPU), which assesses the revenue generated per active unit. It can be quite challenging to measure offline to online conversions from exposure to a DOOH ad , however not impossible with the right partner. Request a demo today to see how Perion can optimize your campaigns. Foot Traffic Foot traffic (also known as footfall traffic) measures the number of visits to a specific point-of-interest (POI) or location such as a physical store as a result of a DOOH campaign. One advantage of DOOH is that advertisers can leverage dynamic creatives to attract customers to the closest store location. Some use cases that can benefit from Foot Traffic studies: Drive intent and action: Use location-based targeting to encourage consumers to visit physical stores after seeing DOOH ads. Generate Foot Traffic: Display relevant messages that create urgency or offer promotions tied to nearby stores. Use big events: You can drive people to your locations around big promotions and store events. Example Case Studies from Perion Bakers Delight: “The Perfect DOOH Recipe”. This programmatic Digital Out‑of‑Home (DOOH) campaign targeted audiences near bakery locations using proximity-based triggers and real-time dynamic creatives. The campaign resulted in a significant uplift in footfall due to precision targeting around store locations. It also leveraged DOOH’s immediacy and location context to drive in-store visits in real time. Tecate & Perion Case Study. Perion partnered with Tecate , a leading light beer brand, to execute a programmatic digital-out-of‑home campaign. The goal was to build brand presence and drive foot traffic using location‑aware messaging and dynamic content tailored to context. It combined dynamic creatives with location intelligence to trigger ads during high‑engagement moments. The campaign resulted in an increase in ad recall, brand preference and brand recognition. Brand Lift Brand studies measure awareness and consideration, making them a valuable top-of-the-funnel metric. Brand lift studies are critical in measuring a campaign’s impact on consumer awareness, consideration, interest, ad recal,l and intent, making them a valuable top-of-the-funnel metric . These studies provide insights into how a target audience perceives a brand after exposure to specific campaigns. Brand studies are especially suitable for specific campaign types. For example, a branding or rebranding campaign can gauge shifts in brand recognition or perception. Product launch studies measure how well a new product enters consumer awareness. Competitive awareness campaigns assess a brand’s standing relative to competitors, and loyalty programs measure how campaigns influence ongoing customer engagement and retention. These studies help marketers optimize future strategies based on data-driven insights. Examples of Successful DOOH Campaign Measurements Measuring DOOH campaigns is as critical to their success as to their execution. Here are some examples of DOOH campaigns that excelled by combining expert targeting and measurement techniques. Lululemon Source: Perion Lululemon aimed to boost brand awareness and drive in-store traffic in Germany. They ran multiple programmatic Digital-Out-of-Home (DOOH) campaigns throughout the year to achieve this. Partnering with Zenith and Hivestack, Lululemon used Brand Lift and Footfall Studies to measure campaign effectiveness. These studies focused on key brand metrics, including awareness, consideration, and favorability, helping Lululemon understand the impact of their campaigns on consumer behavior. One key campaign promoted Lululemon’s shorts using “Custom Audience” targeting females aged 18-34 in health-conscious environments such as gyms and transit stations. Another campaign focused on performance leggings, targeting marathon routes in Munich and Berlin to engage participants and spectators. The results were impressive. For the “performance leggings” campaign, there was a 640% increase in brand image and a 208% increase in interest. The “shorts” campaign saw a 314% boost in foot traffic and 4296 modeled incremental walk-ins. Lululemon continues to optimize its DOOH strategies year-round with Hivestack, driving substantial brand growth and in-store sales. Fiji Airways Source: Perion Fiji Airways, recognized as the “Best Airline in Australia and the Pacific” sought to increase brand awareness and loyalty across multiple global markets . Using programmatic digital-out-of-home (DOOH) advertising, the airline effectively targeted key audiences, including young families and affluent travelers. The campaign ran in markets such as Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, China, Singapore, Japan, Canada, and the U.S. By leveraging demographic and behavioral data and dayparting to display ads during peak times, Fiji Airways ensured maximum relevance and engagement. The agile campaign allowed the airline to adapt creatives across markets in a single day, while also integrating omnichannel retargeting to reinforce its message. Fiji Airways also leveraged measurement techniques such as a Brand Lift study to evaluate the campaign results. The results exceeded expectations, delivering 79 million global impressions – 40% more than anticipated . The Brand Lift Study in China revealed that 77% of respondents recalled outdoor and elevator ads, with 97% associated with Fiji Airways. Furthermore, 76% reported an improved impression of the airline, and 77% expressed an increased intention to fly with them in the future. Retargeting efforts also reduced the cost per acquisition by 300%. Leverage Programmatic DOOH with Perion Source: Perion Enhance your brand’s visibility and engage with your audience at key moments throughout their journey. By utilizing programmatic technology, you gain access to advanced audience targeting, real-time campaign optimization, and flexible ad placements across premium digital screens globally. Our full-funnel measurement solutions, powered by machine learning, allow advertisers to analyze real-time signals, and determine the most effective ad for the audience. With Perion’s cutting-edge platform, you can seamlessly integrate DOOH into your omnichannel strategy for measurable impact. Contact the experts at Perion today to learn how programmatic DOOH can transform your advertising efforts. FAQs How are DOOH impressions calculated? DOOH impressions are typically calculated by estimating the potential number of people in proximity to a DOOH screen at a specific time or period of time. Enhanced through predictive and behavioral data audience concentration numbers can be forecasted prior to a campaign and 3rd party data such as traffic data, location data, and anonymized mobile location data can provide more accurate calculations. Unlike other digital channels that are one-to-one audience numbers, DOOH is a one-to-many channel. How to calculate CPM in DOOH? To calculate CPM (Cost per Mile) for DOOH, we divide the total cost of the ad campaign by the number of impressions (in thousands). The formula is: CPM = ( Total Cost x1000 Impressions) What is the best metric to measure DOOH performance? There is no one perfect approach to DOOH measurement, but a flexible approach that allows marketers and buyers to customize a campaign with their own KPIs – ranging across the entire funnel from awareness to conversion. With the advent of innovative technology and integrated data, OOH is no longer seen as an awareness channel, but also a performance medium for marketers. How effective is DOOH? DOOH is a highly effective medium – unmissable, unskippable and centred around the audience journey outside of the home, perfect for delivering targeted messages in real-time, especially when combined with programmatic techniques. title: Vertiv Ranks Most Critical Industries in the World
summary: Utilities, including electricity, gas, nuclear power and water treatment, are the most critical industries in the world according to a new ranking from Vertiv, formerly Emerson Network Power.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [June 20, 2017] – Utilities, including electricity, gas, nuclear power and water treatment, are the most critical industries in the world according to a new ranking from Vertiv, formerly Emerson Network Power. Vertiv convened a panel of global critical infrastructure experts to systematically quantify and rank the criticality of multiple industries based on 15 criteria. Mass transit—specifically rail and air transportation—ranked second on the list, followed by telecommunications, upstream oil and gas activity and cloud and colocation. The full list is available in a new report, Ranking the World’s Most Critical Industries , released today and available at www.VertivCo.com/MostCritical . The panel set criteria encompassing the range of potential impacts from the loss of availability of critical systems and weighted them based on the severity of the impact. These criteria then were used to create a criticality rubric the panel used to score the industries, which then were ranked by their average scores. “If there is a common theme at the top of this list, it is the interconnectedness of these industries,” said Jack Pouchet, vice president, market development, Vertiv. “These sectors are important to the foundation of today’s society, and downtime in any of these areas can reverberate across industries and around the globe. This will only continue as our world becomes more mobile and more connected and as the Internet of Things expands.” Clean power and water are fundamental needs in a developed society and underpin most other industries and services, making utilities a clear choice as the most critical industry. Mass transit ranked second, with panelists citing not just the safety of travelers, but the massive impact delays and disruptions can have across multiple businesses, markets and the world. The No. 3 ranking for telecommunications reflects the importance of communications and connectivity in personal and business activities and emergency situations. Financial services topped the list of industries ranking highest in terms of financial impact of unplanned downtime. E-commerce was second, followed by cloud and colocation. Cloud and colocation also ranked fifth overall in the list of most critical industries due to the increased dependence on those platforms across multiple businesses. The panel also identified cloud and colocation as one of several rapidly emerging industries that are becoming increasingly critical. “Cloud and colocation growth continues to accelerate,” said panelist Tony Gaunt, senior director for colocation, cloud and banking, financial services and insurance for Vertiv in Asia. “We are right at the beginning of the up curve for core industries’ cloud adoption, and it’s likely that future critical services—the IoT networks that support smart cities and manufacturing, for example—will develop in the cloud.” The full list of critical industries as well as the analysis of specific categories, emerging industries and the ranking methodology are available in the report, Ranking the World’s Most Critical Industries . To see how other industries rank, use the Criticality Calculator . For more information on technologies and solutions to ensure network availability and additional content from Vertiv, visit www.VertivCo.com/MostCritical . About Vertiv Vertiv designs, builds and services critical infrastructure that enables vital applications for data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities. Formerly Emerson Network Power, Vertiv supports today’s growing mobile and cloud computing markets with a portfolio of power, thermal and infrastructure management solutions including the ASCO®, Chloride®, Liebert®, NetSure™ and Trellis™ brands. Sales in fiscal 2016 were $4.4 billion. For more information, visit VertivCo.com. CONTACT: Vince McMorrow T +614 383 1622 E Vince.McMorrow@Fahlgren.com

title: Top 10 ATS and CRM Platforms for Recruiting Agencies in 2026
summary: We compared 10 ATS and CRM platforms for recruiting agencies. AI capabilities, pricing, migration speed, and what actually matters for placements in 2026.
body_text: We compared the major platforms so you don't have to. Here's what actually matters. TLDR Spott leads for AI-native depth, with in-house migration in a day to a few weeks, depending on database size and feedback speed Bullhorn remains the default for large enterprises with deep ecosystems Loxo and Manatal offer the most accessible entry points (free tier and $15/user/month) Ezekia is the specialist pick for retained executive search Vincere and Tracker RMS stand out for contract and temp desks needing operational tools Full comparison table and decision framework below. Every recruiting agency runs on its ATS and CRM. Your applicant tracking system manages the candidate pipeline. Your CRM handles client relationships and business development. Most modern platforms combine both into one system. And whichever one you pick will shape how your team works every single day. The problem is that the market has become almost impossible to navigate. Dozens of vendors all claim to be the best fit for agencies. Legacy platforms are bolting on AI features to stay relevant. Newer entrants are shipping fast but lack depth. And the difference between a platform that's truly AI-native (built around AI from day one) versus one that's just AI-powered (AI added after the fact) is the kind of thing that only shows up after you've already committed. We cut through the noise. Here's what we found. What to Look For in an ATS/CRM in 2026 Before diving into the list, here are the five criteria that separate strong platforms from weak ones this year: AI depth, not AI marketing. Every vendor says "AI-powered" now. The question is whether AI is baked into the architecture or bolted on as a feature . Purpose-built AI transforms workflows. Retrofitted AI saves you a few clicks. Unified ATS + CRM. Running separate systems for candidate tracking and client management creates data silos. The best platforms unify both so every recruiter sees the full picture. Migration speed. Switching platforms shouldn't take four months and a consulting engagement. Ask every vendor: how long until we're fully operational? Workflow fit. Generic CRM patterns don't match how recruiters actually work. Look for platforms designed around the recruit-to-placement lifecycle, not adapted from sales or HR tools. Pricing that scales. Per-user pricing punishes growth. Understand the total cost at 10, 25, and 50 users before committing. The Top 10 1. Spott Best for: Agencies that want AI working for them, not just available to them Spott is an AI-native ATS/CRM built from the ground up for recruiting and staffing agencies. Unlike platforms that added AI as an afterthought, Spott's entire architecture is designed around intelligence, capturing context from calls, messages, and notes to surface candidates and insights automatically. What stands out: AI matching that actually works. Spott doesn't just keyword-match. It understands context: skills, conversations, hiring patterns. It surfaces candidates that fit. One customer described the precision as something that "stood out immediately." Migration handled in-house. Spott's AI-powered migration gets most agencies fully operational in a day to a few weeks, depending on database size and feedback speed, including data cleanup and enrichment. Conversation memory. Through Unibox, Spott captures and retains context from every interaction: calls, emails, messages. Nothing falls through the cracks. Your ATS remembers what you discussed, not just what you entered. Speed to presentation. Recruiters can rapidly share top candidates with clients. As one agency put it, the speed "makes the whole process feel effortless." Recruiter-first design. Every workflow is built around how recruiters actually operate, from sourcing to placement, rather than forcing a generic CRM pattern. Credibility: Y Combinator backed. $3.2M seed round. ISO 27001 certified. GDPR compliant with EU-hosted option. Customers on every continent. Pricing: Available on request via spott.io/pricing . Who it's best for: Agencies with 5-200 recruiters who want a modern, AI-native platform that actively drives placements. Not just stores data. 2. Bullhorn Best for: Large staffing enterprises that prioritize ecosystem breadth over innovation speed Bullhorn is the incumbent. With 25+ years in the market and 10,000+ customers, it's the default at many of the industry's largest staffing firms. What stands out: Massive integration ecosystem with 300+ marketplace integrations Strong automation for high-volume staffing workflows Passive communication tracking through Gmail and Outlook integration Dedicated VMS integration tools for enterprise staffing The trade-off: Bullhorn's size is both its strength and its limitation. The core dates to 1999 and has grown by acquisition (Herefish, cube19, Textkernel), so automation, analytics, and AI live as separate add-on products rather than one system. G2 reviewers regularly cite slow load times and a dense interface, and enterprise rollouts are typically consultant-assisted. Pricing: Starter $99/user/mo and Core $165/user/mo are published (July 2026); the Pro tier, automation, analytics, and Amplify AI are quote-only add-ons, so real-world totals land above the sticker price. Who it's best for: Large agencies (100+ recruiters) already embedded in the Bullhorn ecosystem, or enterprises where the integration marketplace is a requirement. 3. Loxo Best for: Executive search firms and small agencies that want sourcing and ATS in one place Loxo combines ATS, CRM, and an extensive sourcing database in a single platform. The free tier makes it accessible for solo recruiters and small shops, and the sourcing capabilities (pulling from LinkedIn, GitHub, and other networks) are genuinely strong. What stands out: Free-forever ATS and CRM tier Large talent database aggregating multiple professional networks AI candidate matching that surfaces relevant profiles Outreach sequences built into the platform The trade-off: Loxo works well for smaller operations, but agencies scaling past 20-30 recruiters often find the workflows limiting. Enterprise-grade customization and reporting depth don't match what larger firms need. The AI, while useful, is more of a feature layer than an architectural foundation. Pricing: Free tier available. Paid plans with additional features. Contact Loxo for details. Who it's best for: Executive search firms and small-to-mid agencies (under 25 recruiters) that prioritize sourcing capabilities. 4. JobAdder Best for: Agencies in the UK and Australia that want a flexible, no-lock-in ATS/CRM JobAdder is a cloud-based ATS and CRM that's earned a loyal following, particularly among agencies in the UK and Australia. Launched in 2007 and trusted by 26,000+ users, it hits a practical middle ground: broad enough to handle most agency workflows, straightforward enough that teams adopt it quickly. What stands out: No lock-in contracts. Month-to-month billing with no penalty fees to switch. That's rare in this market. 200+ job board integrations and 150+ technology partners for a flexible, modular tech stack 60+ built-in reports and dashboards. One of the more comprehensive out of the box analytics offerings Multi-channel candidate engagement (email, SMS, WhatsApp) with bulk messaging up to 500 profiles AI enhancements through Adder Intelligence: smart summaries, smart sync, smart job descriptions The trade-off: JobAdder is a solid generalist, but it's not the deepest platform in any single area. Users report navigation issues and note that advanced reporting still falls short for some workflows. User management requires support intervention for basic admin tasks, and there's no free trial to test-drive before committing. Pricing has also been trending upward. Pricing: Starts at approximately $160/user/month. Custom quotes based on team size and needs. Who it's best for: Agencies (10-50 recruiters) in the UK and Australia that value flexibility, no long-term contracts, and a broad integration ecosystem. 5. Recruit CRM Best for: Global agencies that need invoicing, stakeholder feedback, and multi-currency support Recruit CRM delivers a solid ATS/CRM combo with features that go beyond candidate management. Built-in invoicing, client feedback tools, and revenue dashboards make it a practical choice for agencies managing the full business cycle. What stands out: Built-in invoicing and revenue tracking by client and recruiter Stakeholder feedback tools for candidate submissions Effort-to-revenue dashboards for measuring ROI Frequent feature updates driven by user requests Transparent pricing with no hidden costs The trade-off: While Recruit CRM covers a lot of ground, its AI capabilities aren't as deep as purpose-built platforms. The platform serves a broad market, which means agency-specific workflows can feel generic in places. Advanced automation requires the higher-tier plans. Pricing: Pro at $85/user/month. Business at $125/user/month. Enterprise at $165/user/month (billed annually). Who it's best for: Global agencies that need business operations features (invoicing, reporting) alongside their ATS/CRM. 6. Ezekia Best for: Executive search firms that need a purpose-built CRM with fast onboarding Ezekia is built specifically for executive search. Not adapted from a generic ATS or CRM. Trusted by 550+ firms globally with a 99.7% customer retention rate over seven years, it focuses on what retained search firms actually need: assignment management, business development tracking, client portals, and branded reporting. What stands out: Purpose-built for executive search. Workflows designed around retained, interim, and in-house assignments. Not generic recruiting patterns. Fast onboarding. Teams get up and running in hours, not months. Unlimited human support with no ticket queues. Branded client reporting. Automated Word/Excel reports shared through a secure client portal with built-in feedback capture. Business development module. Track opportunities, map relationships, and manage your BD pipeline alongside active assignments. OpenAI-powered features for generating insights, writing summaries, and automating tasks ISO certified. 8,000+ integrations via Zapier. Multi-language support (English, French, German, Portuguese, Spanish). The trade-off: Ezekia is purpose-built for executive search, which means it's not the right fit for high-volume staffing or temp agencies. Reporting and automation features are adequate but don't match the depth of broader platforms. As firms scale beyond retained search into other business models, they may outgrow the platform. Pricing: Starts at £120/month. Flexible monthly subscription with no long-term contracts. Free trial available. Who it's best for: Retained executive search firms and boutique search practices that want a clean, fast, search-specific CRM without the overhead of a platform built for a different business model. 7. Vincere Best for: Large agencies that need a front-to-back office system covering recruitment through payroll Vincere positions itself as the operating system for recruitment agencies, handling everything from ATS and CRM to timesheets, invoicing, and analytics in a single platform. It covers permanent, contract, and temp staffing models. What stands out: Comprehensive front-to-back office: ATS, CRM, timesheets, invoicing, analytics Strong support for contract and temp staffing (time management, billing) Built-in candidate and client portals Detailed analytics dashboards for agency operations The trade-off: Vincere's breadth means complexity. Smaller agencies often find it overpowered for their needs. The platform's architecture hasn't kept pace with newer competitors on the AI front, and the interface can feel dated compared to more modern tools. Pricing: Contact vendor. Generally mid-to-high range. Who it's best for: Mid-to-large agencies (25+ recruiters) running contract/temp desks that need operational tools (timesheets, billing) integrated with their ATS/CRM. 8. Recruiterflow Best for: Small-to-mid agencies looking for AI-forward features at a reasonable price Recruiterflow markets itself as an AI-first ATS and CRM built for recruiting agencies and executive search firms. The platform bundles ATS, CRM, outreach sequencing, data enrichment, and AI agents into a unified experience with visual Kanban-style pipeline management. What stands out: AI agents for automating routine recruiting tasks Built-in outreach sequencing and data enrichment Visual Kanban boards for pipeline management Clean, modern interface that's quick to adopt Focused specifically on agency workflows The trade-off: Recruiterflow serves a wide range of agency sizes but can lack depth in enterprise features. Advanced reporting, role-based permissions, and compliance tools aren't as mature as larger platforms. Integration ecosystem is smaller than Bullhorn or JobAdder. Pricing: Contact vendor for current plans. Who it's best for: Small-to-mid agencies (5-40 recruiters) that want a modern, focused ATS/CRM without the overhead of enterprise platforms. 9. Manatal Best for: Budget-conscious agencies that want AI capabilities without breaking the bank Manatal is one of the most affordable ATS/CRM platforms with genuine AI features. Starting at $15/user/month, it's accessible to agencies that can't justify enterprise pricing. The platform includes AI-driven candidate recommendations, resume parsing, and integrations with 2,500+ job boards. What stands out: Aggressive pricing: starts at $15/user/month (billed annually) AI candidate recommendations and scoring 2,500+ job board integrations Social media profile enrichment (LinkedIn + 20 platforms) 14-day free trial, no credit card required The trade-off: You get what you pay for in certain areas. Reporting is basic compared to mid-market and enterprise tools. Resume parsing accuracy can be inconsistent. Customization options for workflows and dashboards are limited. The mobile experience works but isn't polished. Pricing: Professional at $15/user/month. Enterprise at $35/user/month. Enterprise Plus at $55/user/month (all billed annually). Who it's best for: Small agencies (under 15 recruiters) and solo recruiters who need a functional ATS/CRM with AI features at a budget-friendly price. 10. Tracker RMS Best for: Growing agencies that need strong CRM and ATS integration with operational tools Tracker RMS has been serving staffing agencies since 2005 and excels at seamless CRM/ATS integration. Its strength is reducing the friction between business development and recruiting. Your sales pipeline and candidate pipeline live in the same system with no data gaps. What stands out: Tight CRM/ATS integration. Sales and recruitment data flows seamlessly AI-powered candidate ranking based on engagement and profile data Built-in marketing campaigns (email and text) Operational tools: timesheets, expenses, onboarding, accounting integration VMS automation for enterprise staffing Deep integration library (LinkedIn Recruiter, Indeed, QuickBooks, and more) The trade-off: Tracker's depth requires commitment. The learning curve for advanced features is real. The interface doesn't feel as modern as newer competitors. Financial tracking, while comprehensive, is described by some users as overly complex. Pricing isn't publicly listed. Pricing: Contact vendor. Generally competitive for the feature set. Who it's best for: Growing agencies (10-50 recruiters) that need their sales and recruiting operations in one system, especially those running contract and temp desks. Quick Comparison Table Platform Best For AI Matching Integrated Notetaker Starting Price Spott #1 AI-native agencies (5-200 recruiters) ✓ Vector database: searches across calls, notes, messages, and CVs ✓ Teams, Zoom, Google Meet, mobile app, VOIP Contact sales Bullhorn Large enterprises (100+) ~ Keyword-based + add-on AI layer ~ Via third-party integrations Starter $99 / Core $165 published; Pro and add-ons quote-only Loxo Small agencies and exec search ~ AI matching on structured profile data ✓ Zoom & Teams Contact sales JobAdder UK/AU agencies (10-50) ~ Adder Intelligence on structured fields ~ Via third-party integrations ~$160/user/month Recruit CRM Global agencies needing invoicing ~ AI recommendations on structured data ~ Via third-party integrations $85/user/month Ezekia Retained executive search ~ OpenAI-powered suggestions ✕ Not available £120/month Vincere Contract/temp desks (25+) ✕ Keyword search only ~ Via third-party integrations Contact vendor Recruiterflow Small-to-mid agencies (5-40) ~ AI agents on structured data ✓ Zoom, Meet & Teams Contact vendor Manatal Budget-conscious small teams ~ AI scoring on structured data ~ Native notetaker (Beta) $15/user/month Tracker RMS Growing agencies (10-50) ~ AI ranking on structured data ~ Via third-party integrations Contact vendor How to Choose There's no universally "best" ATS/CRM. The right platform depends on your agency's size, business model, and priorities. Here's a framework: If AI is your top priority: Spott is the only platform on this list built from the ground up as an AI-native system. Every other vendor is adding AI to an existing product. The architectural difference shows up in how the platform handles matching, context capture, and workflow automation. If you're a large enterprise locked into an ecosystem: Bullhorn's integration marketplace is unmatched. If your tech stack already runs through Bullhorn, the switching cost is high and the ecosystem value is real. If budget drives your decision: Manatal at $15/user/month and Loxo's free tier give you functional ATS/CRM capabilities at a fraction of the cost. You'll trade depth and customization for accessibility. If you run contract/temp desks: Vincere and Tracker RMS offer operational tools (timesheets, invoicing, billing) that most ATS/CRM platforms don't include natively. If you run a retained executive search practice: Ezekia is purpose-built for your business model. Assignment management, client portals, and BD tracking without the noise of features designed for temp and volume staffing. If you need to switch fast: Ask every vendor about migration timelines. Some agencies spend months in transition limbo. Spott handles migration in-house with AI data migration tools; most agencies are live in a day to a few weeks, depending on database size and feedback speed. The Bottom Line The ATS/CRM market in 2026 is splitting into two camps : legacy platforms adding AI features to stay competitive, and modern platforms built with AI at the core. Legacy systems still dominate by installed base, but the gap between what recruiters need and what these platforms deliver grows every quarter. AI matching, conversation memory, automated data enrichment, and intelligent workflow automation aren't nice-to-haves anymore. They're the baseline for competitive agencies. The agencies that switch to AI-native tools now will compound that advantage over the next few years. The ones that wait will spend more time catching up than recruiting. Choose accordingly. title: The PIM Space Is Evolving At The Speed Of AI
summary: Explore how AI, governance, and rising business demands are reshaping the product information management market.
body_text: Earlier this year, I had the opportunity to take over coverage of the product information management (PIM) space from my colleague Chuck Gahun , and it has been a fascinating journey. I’ve immersed myself in myriad vendor briefings, dug into historical and more recent Forrester research, and educated myself on the history of the space and its evolution. The PIM space has transformed well beyond its roots as a back-office data repository. Today, it plays a central role in how organizations manage, govern, and activate product data across increasingly complex digital ecosystems. The market has evolved to meet the needs of commerce leaders who are looking for vendors that effectively enable controlled, scalable product data in an AI-driven world. What Are Some Common Themes? AI continues to redefine how PIM creates value. To no surprise of anyone remotely connected with the commerce space, AI continues to reshape the direction of the PIM market. Yet the conversation has evolved beyond simply adding AI capabilities. Organizations increasingly seek to balance speed and scale with human oversight, reliability, and accountability. Rising expectations are redefining product information management. Commercial and technology forces are raising expectations for how product information is managed. Regulatory requirements necessitate increased transparency, traceability, and control. At the same time, segment boundaries are blurring as platforms, partners, and surrounding technologies grow more interconnected. These realities impact how organizations think about product information, with the focus shifting from intrinsic capabilities to broader ecosystem information flow. PIM value is shifting from features to orchestration. While the foundational functionality of PIM is still key, differentiation is increasingly moving toward how effectively platforms support coordination, governance, and interoperability. Also, competitive pressure is evidenced not only in AI capabilities but also from adjacent technologies, evolving buyer expectations, and changing product optimization approaches. The market is being redefined around adaptability, control, and effective operation across expanding networks of systems, data, and stakeholders. What To Watch For In the landscape report, I’ll highlight the major trends, but what stands out is the broader pattern. There is evidence of an industry shift where there is a blend of innovation with control, expansion with discipline, and ambition with caution — with variations between the players. There’s a lot more beneath the surface of these signals, and the full landscape report will unpack the latest on the space and its vendors. If you’re evaluating PIM, rethinking your product data strategy, or trying to understand how these shifts apply to your organization, I’d welcome a conversation . Share

title: Open enrollment best practices: planning a smoother season
summary: How to plan a smoother open enrollment: timeline, communications, and the prep that prevents last-minute scrambles.
body_text: Open enrollment runs smoother when the work starts months before the window opens. Really, it comes down to four things: a clear timeline, communication that doesn’t stop after November, education built from the actual plans, and some way to measure what employees actually understood. Get those in place, and employees make better choices, HR fields fewer last-minute questions, and the consultant looks like the person who kept the season calm. This open enrollment guide walks through what prevents the annual scramble and where the right tools can take the manual work off your plate. What is an open enrollment best practice? Open enrollment best practices are the planning, communication, and education steps that help employees choose the right coverage with less confusion and less pressure on HR. They turn open enrollment from a two-week fire drill into a repeatable process. In practice: start early, write in plain language all year, make the plan differences easy to see, and track engagement so you know what to fix before the next renewal. Why open enrollment best practices matter now Two pressures collide every fall: cost and confusion. On cost, KFF reported that average annual premiums for employer-sponsored family coverage reached $26,993 in 2025, up 6% from the prior year.1 Employees feel those increases in every paycheck, which raises the stakes on the choices they make at enrollment. On confusion, Aflac’s 2024–2025 WorkForces Report found that 51% of employees still didn’t fully understand their health insurance, and 71% wanted more information about their benefits.2 When people don’t understand their options, they default to last year’s plan or the lowest paycheck deduction, and the questions land on HR during the busiest weeks of the year. The practices below close that gap before the enrollment window opens. Start the open enrollment timeline early The single biggest predictor of a smooth season is how early you start. Teams that wait until the window opens spend the whole season catching up. A workable open enrollment timeline builds backward from the enrollment dates: lock plan decisions and rates first, then build materials, then communicate, then enroll, then follow up. Timeframe Focus Who owns it 3–4 months out Finalize plan design, rates, and carrier decisions Consultant + HR 6–8 weeks out Build guides, microsites, and decision support from final plan data Consultant + HR + AI agents 2–3 weeks out Launch OE reminder communications across email, SMS, and meetings HR + AI agents Enrollment window Answer questions fast and keep all materials in one place HR + AI assistant After close Review engagement data, send post-close comms, and note what to fix next year Consultant + HR + AI agents Communicate year-round, not only during the window The most common open enrollment mistake is treating communication as a two-week event. People need to see information several times before it sticks, and a single newsletter during the enrollment window won’t get there. Steady, relevant communication across the year means employees arrive at enrollment already informed. Pasito helps benefits teams run that cadence with year-round communications and benefits microsites that pull from the same plan data, so the website, emails, and guides always say the same thing. Make plan choices easy to understand Employees can’t choose well if they can’t tell the plans apart. Clear benefit guides and decision support translate deductibles, copays, networks, and prescription rules into a side-by-side choice people can actually make. When the education is grounded in the actual plan, employees stop guessing and start comparing. Cut the repetitive question load Most open enrollment questions are simple to answer. They just all arrive at once, and each one feels urgent to the person asking. “Is my doctor in network? Can I add my spouse? Where’s my HSA info?” An AI Benefits Assistant trained on the actual plan documents can answer those instantly, with the right tone and source controls, so HR isn’t answering the same five questions a hundred times. Measure what employees understand Most teams end the season with opinions about what worked. But relying on the data’s a better and more sure approach. Track which guides and pages employees view, which questions they ask, and where they get stuck. That tells consultants and HR exactly what to fix before the next renewal, so each season starts a little further ahead than the last. Turn open enrollment best practices into a year-round process These open enrollment best practices share one idea: the season goes well because the work starts long before the window opens. Plan early, communicate all year, make the choices clear, answer questions fast, and measure what lands. HR gets a calmer season, employees make better decisions, and consultants prove their value when it counts. Pasito gives consultants and HR teams one workspace to plan, build, communicate, and measure benefits all year, so open enrollment stops being a season and starts being a checkpoint. ‍ FAQ What are open enrollment best practices? Open enrollment best practices are the planning, communication, and education steps that help employees choose the right coverage with less confusion: starting early, communicating year-round in plain language, making plan differences clear, and measuring engagement. When should open enrollment planning start? Lock plan decisions and rates three to four months before the enrollment window, then build materials and communications in the weeks that follow. Starting that early is what prevents the last-minute scramble. How can HR reduce open enrollment questions? Communicate consistently before the window, give employees plan-accurate guides and decision support, and use an AI benefits assistant trained on the actual plans to answer common questions instantly. ‍ References 1. KFF, “2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey.” https://www.kff.org/health-costs/2025-employer-health-benefits-survey/ 2. Aflac, “2024–2025 Aflac WorkForces Report: The state of workplace benefits and employee engagement.” https://www.aflac.com/docs/awr/pdf/2024-trends-and-topics/2024-aflac-awr-the-state-of-workplace-benefits-and-enrollment.pdf ‍

title: Ask an Advisor: ‘I’m So Lost.’ Should I Roll My Old 401(k) into My Current Plan or Convert it to a Roth IRA?
summary: You’ll owe income tax on the money if you move it into a Roth IRA, but that doesn’t necessarily mean it's a bad idea.
body_text: I’m so lost: I have a 401(k) that’s sitting doing nothing. I have not transferred the funds to my new employer ‘ s 401(k) because I’m not sure it’s the best decision. I’m thinking of transferring funds into a Roth IRA but I’m afraid it will affect our tax bracket because I’m sure we will have to pay the IRS. – Liliana You are correct that you’ll owe income tax on the money if you move it into a Roth IRA , but that doesn’t necessarily mean it’s a bad idea. Leaving it where it is or moving it into your new employer’s plan could also be good moves. Let’s take a look at your options to see which might be best for you. Not sure whether tax-deferred or Roth savings make more sense? A financial advisor can help you compare your options and build a retirement strategy around your goals. Leaving It Where It Is This is the simplest approach in the short run, but there are some downsides. The main one is that it’s another account to keep track of. That could be an extra hassle going forward and it’s not likely to give you any additional benefit. You mention that it’s “doing nothing.” In my experience, this usually means you haven’t invested your money or you’re holding very conservative investments that provide little growth potential. If you decide to keep it where it is, make sure you review your investment choices and select investments that align with your goals and risk tolerance. Another thing to keep in mind is that some employer plans charge higher fees than others. It’s worth reviewing the fees and investment options available to make sure the plan is still a good fit. You can typically find this information in your plan’s fee disclosure documents, online account portal or fund fact sheets, which may show administrative fees, expense ratios and other plan costs. Rolling It Into Your New Employer’s Plan This should be fairly straightforward. You may need to fill out some paperwork or simply contact the financial institution that manages your old employer’s plan and tell them where to transfer the money. The biggest advantage to a rollover is simplicity. Having your retirement savings in one workplace plan makes it easier to manage and monitor your progress. In some cases, your new plan may also offer lower costs or better investment options than your old one. There can be another benefit as well. If you retire after age 55 but before age 59 ½, money in your current employer’s 401(k) may be eligible for penalty-free withdrawals under a special IRS exception. That rule generally doesn’t apply to money held in an IRA, so it can be worth considering if early retirement is a possibility. (Work with a financial advisor to create a retirement plan that converts your 401(k)s, IRAs and other assets into a sustainable income stream.) Click Your State to Get Matched With Financial Advisors That Serve Your Area Choose your state and answer some questions to get matched with up to three fiduciary advisors that serve your area. Converting It to a Roth IRA This option may make sense depending on your current tax rate and the balance in the account. When you convert pre-tax 401(k) money to a Roth IRA, the amount converted is added to your taxable income for the year. That means a large conversion could increase your tax bill significantly. A Roth conversion can increase your taxable income enough to move part of it into a higher tax bracket . However, the higher rate only applies to the income within that bracket, not your entire income. Even with that distinction, it’s worth estimating the tax bill before converting so you know what to expect. A Roth IRA can offer tax-free income in retirement, as long as withdrawals meet the qualified distribution rules. It also gives account owners more control over timing, since Roth IRAs do not require lifetime RMDs . For someone who expects higher tax rates later, converting now and paying the tax bill upfront may reduce taxes over time. You don’t necessarily have to convert the entire balance at once, either. Some people choose to convert smaller amounts over several years to spread out the tax cost and avoid pushing too much income into higher tax brackets. (And if you want help planning a Roth conversion, speak with a financial advisor about your unique situation.) Another Option: A Traditional IRA One option you didn’t mention is rolling the old 401(k) into a traditional IRA. This allows you to keep the tax-deferred status of the account without creating a current tax bill. A traditional IRA may also provide a much wider range of investment choices than most employer-sponsored retirement plans. For some investors, that flexibility is a major advantage. If you expect to do Roth conversions in the future, moving money into a traditional IRA can make that easier. That’s because you don’t have to navigate employer plan rules to do it. Bottom Line Roth ira conversion memo near retro briefcase and glasses. There isn’t a single right answer. The best choice depends on factors such as your current tax bracket, expected future tax rates, investment preferences and how important simplicity is to you. If paying a large tax bill today would be difficult, a full Roth conversion may not make sense right now. On the other hand, if your income is temporarily lower than usual, converting some or all of the account could be worth considering. Before making a decision, compare the fees and investment options in your old plan to your new employer’s plan and any IRA you’re considering. Taking time to evaluate those differences can help you choose the option that best supports your retirement strategy. Retirement Planning Tips Finding a financial advisor doesn’t have to be hard. SmartAsset’s free tool matches you with vetted financial advisors who serve your area, and you can have a free introductory call with your advisor matches to decide which one you feel is right for you. If you’re ready to find an advisor who can help you achieve your financial goals, get started now . Review whether your portfolio is built for withdrawals, not just growth. A portfolio that worked while you were saving may not be ideal once you begin taking income from it . Before retirement, consider whether your investments can support regular withdrawals, manage market declines and provide enough liquidity so you are not forced to sell long-term assets at the wrong time. title: Viasat demonstrates first integrated automotive satellite voice call capability with BMW Group
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Viasat, Inc.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: Press Release Facebook LinkedIn Twitter RSS << Back Jul 16, 2026 Viasat demonstrates first integrated automotive satellite voice call capability with BMW Group PDF Version Viasat experts demonstrate satellite-enabled voice call capabilities as part of research collaboration during this week’s 5G Automotive Association Meeting Week in Munich, Germany: for the first time integrated with the infotainment system of a BMW iX3. Showcase highlights what might be possible in future and the potential for reliable voice and messaging connectivity beyond the reach of traditional terrestrial networks. MUNICH, July 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Viasat, Inc. (NASDAQ: VSAT), a global leader in satellite communications, today announced a landmark technology demonstration showcasing the first automotive satellite voice call demonstration fully integrated into a BMW Group vehicle’s platform. It marks a significant step forward as Viasat brings Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) communications into the connected vehicle ecosystem: enabling drivers and passengers to stay connected in remote or underserved areas where cellular coverage may be limited or unavailable. Building on an earlier demonstration with eSIM capabilities from Cubic³, a leading provider of software-defined vehicle (SDV) solutions, Viasat experts in Munich utilized advanced technology including Qualcomm Technologies Inc.’s Snapdragon® Auto 5G Modem-RF Gen 2 solution, and the Fraunhofer IIS NESC AI voice codec. This enables voice communications to be sent using the NB-IoT communications protocol over Viasat’s highly reliable, L-band satellite network. For the first time, this technology was integrated with BMW Group’s in-vehicle architecture, allowing voice calls to be initiated and managed directly through the vehicle interface. By extending messaging and voice services beyond cellular coverage, automakers like BMW Group can ensure drivers remain connected for emergency assistance and critical safety applications, regardless of location. “This demonstration reflects broader industry excitement to ensure consistent, resilient satellite capabilities for next-generation vehicles,” said Sandeep Moorthy, Senior Vice President, Advanced Non-Terrestrial Solutions at Viasat. “By bringing standards-based NTN to vehicles, we can integrate satellite voice and messaging and ultimately enable a future where drivers can remain connected — wherever the journey takes them.” Viasat, BMW Group, Cubic3, and Fraunhofer IIS are active members of the 5GAA (5G Automotive Association) , which brings together technology and automotive partners to develop real-world, scalable connectivity solutions for all road users. Satellite-enabled automotive connectivity applications include voice and messaging emergency services, fleet management, and over-the-air updates in low-connectivity regions. The NB-IoT protocol, which can support lower data-rate applications, is enabled by global 3GPP standards. Future releases are expected to pave the way for 5G-New Radio (5G-NR) satellite services, which could support video streaming and seamless roaming between terrestrial and satellite networks. About Viasat Viasat is a global communications company that believes everyone and everything in the world can be connected. With offices in 24 countries around the world, our mission shapes how consumers, businesses, governments and militaries around the world communicate and connect. Viasat is developing the ultimate global communications network to power high-quality, reliable, secure, affordable, fast connections to positively impact people’s lives anywhere they are - on the ground, in the air or at sea, while building a sustainable future in space. In May 2023, Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, combining the teams, technologies and resources of the two companies to create a new global communications partner. title: SEALSQ and GlobalFoundries Partner to Accelerate Post-Quantum Cryptography and Quantum Computing Technologies
summary: SEALSQ and GlobalFoundries have partnered to advance Post-Quantum Cryptography and quantum computing technologies, focusing on secure semiconductor solutions.
body_text: Geneva, Switzerland, July 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SEALSQ Corp (Nasdaq: LAES) ("SEALSQ") and GlobalFoundries (Nasdaq: GFS) (GF) today announced a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to co-develop across secure semiconductor platforms, Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and emerging semiconductor-based quantum computing technologies. The partnership leverages GF's process technology leadership and manufacturing capabilities alongside SEALSQ's expertise in hardware-based certified security, PQC-ready silicon solutions and ongoing investments in quantum technologies. Semiconductor CMOS technology has powered the digital revolution for decades by enabling continuous transistor scaling, higher integration density, and cost-effective mass production. It is now emerging as a key enabler of the quantum era, allowing quantum processors to be built on proven high-volume semiconductor manufacturing platforms that deliver the scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency required for widespread industrial adoption. The collaboration will focus on developing Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) security IP, secure chiplet architectures, and a CryoCMOS ecosystem to support future quantum computing systems, advancing three strategic areas: Expanding GF's IP Ecosystem with Certified PQC Security Building Blocks In partnership with MIPS, a GF company, the companies will co-develop pre-certified PQC security IP (hard macro) blocks and Chiplet Hardware Security Module (CHSM) components, targeting applications including Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) and Secure Enclaves. Advancing Cryogenic CMOS for Quantum Computing Building on GF's recently announced Quantum Technology Solutions business and SEALSQ's ongoing ambitions in quantum ASIC design, the companies will collaborate on the design and development of cryoelectronic ASICs operating at ultra-low temperatures for joint clients and partners, leveraging GF’s U.S. manufacturing capabilities and footprint. Aligned with Sovereign and Trusted Supply Chain Objectives The partnership is designed to support European and U.S. sovereign supply chain priorities. Both companies share a commitment to trusted, traceable, and secure semiconductor production. “A shared long-term vision between GF and SEALSQ is that semiconductors, cybersecurity, Post-Quantum Cryptography, and quantum computing are converging into a single technology ecosystem,” said Carlos Moreira, CEO of SEALSQ . “GlobalFoundries is one of the world’s leading semiconductor manufacturers, and its growing commitment to security and quantum technologies perfectly complements SEALSQ’s expertise in secure semiconductors, PQC, and our investments across the quantum ecosystem. This partnership is a natural fit and a powerful validation of our shared vision. Together, we have the opportunity to help shape the secure and scalable technology platforms that will power the quantum era.” “This partnership is about building the foundation for the quantum era: trusted digital infrastructure secured by Post-Quantum Cryptography and the semiconductor technologies that will enable future quantum computing systems,” said Nicholas Sergeant, vice president of Quantum Technology Solutions at GF . “SEALSQ's secure-semiconductor and Post-Quantum Cryptography expertise complements GF's differentiated technology portfolio and expanding quantum capabilities. Together, we are uniquely positioned to give customers and partners the technologies needed to secure and enable the quantum future.” The initiative builds on GF’s long-standing investments in quantum technologies and complements its new Quantum Technology Solutions business alongside SEALSQ’s investments in quantum computing, reinforcing the critical role of semiconductors in enabling scalable and commercially viable quantum systems. About SEALSQ: SEALSQ is a leading innovator in Post-Quantum Technology hardware and software solutions. Our technology seamlessly integrates Semiconductors, PKI (Public Key Infrastructure), and Provisioning Services, with a strategic emphasis on developing state-of-the-art Quantum Resistant Cryptography and Semiconductors designed to address the urgent security challenges posed by quantum computing. As quantum computers advance, traditional cryptographic methods like RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) are increasingly vulnerable. SEALSQ is pioneering the development of Post-Quantum Semiconductors that provide robust, future-proof protection for sensitive data across a wide range of applications, including Multi-Factor Authentication tokens, Smart Energy, Medical and Healthcare Systems, Defense, IT Network Infrastructure, Automotive, and Industrial Automation and Control Systems. By embedding Post-Quantum Cryptography into our semiconductor solutions, SEALSQ ensures that organizations stay protected against quantum threats. Our products are engineered to safeguard critical systems, enhancing resilience and security across diverse industries. For more information on our Post-Quantum Semiconductors and security solutions, please visit www.sealsq.com . About GF GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high-growth markets. With global manufacturing operations across the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF's talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com . title: The Yinglings: six generations on the rails
body_text: In Altoona, Pa., generations of the Yingling family have worked across the region’s rail shops for more than a century. Today, that legacy continues at Juniata Locomotive Shop , where David “Dave” Yingling Jr., machinist and team leader at Norfolk Southern, is part of that ongoing story. A fifth-generation railroader, Yingling hired on with Conrail in 1993 and has built a career spanning more than three decades across multiple shops and roles. That legacy now extends to the next generation, as his twin sons, Joshua and Jacob Yingling, both machinists, represent the sixth generation working for the railroad. “I was probably 12 when I first walked into the shops, and I was just amazed,” Yingling said. “The scale, the efficiency, everything about it just stuck with me.” From early curiosity to service and skill That early experience sparked a fascination with machines that shaped his path forward. Yingling went on to serve in the U.S. Navy as a hull technician, where he developed welding and mechanical skills through hands-on experience. Within weeks of returning home from active duty, he began his machinist career in Altoona, putting those skills to work in an environment that felt familiar from a young age. His curiosity continues to shape the work as evolving systems, software, and diagnostics change how equipment is maintained and returned to service. A legacy that still guides the work Railroading spans every generation of the Yingling family, with each generation shaping how the next approaches the work. On the overhaul line, that perspective is reflected in how locomotives are stripped, rebuilt, and tested before returning to service. Each stage depends on coordination, precision, and trust across the team to ensure equipment is returned safely and reliably. “It takes everybody working together,” Yingling said. “If we don’t get it right, it impacts more than just us. It impacts the railroad and the country.” Over time, those lessons were reinforced through family stories. Yingling’s grandfather often reminded the family that the railroad plays an essential role beyond the shop, supporting industries and communities across the network. Dave's uncle Denny (left), grandfather Clair (center) and dad David Sr. (back right). Putting leadership into practice As a team leader, Yingling brings that mindset into how he works with his team. His father, a former carman gang leader, prepared him for the realities of representing both frontline employees and leadership expectations. “He told me you’ve got to be able to handle both sides,” Yingling said. “You have to respect people, stay professional, and make sure messages flow either way.” In practice, that guidance shows up in his focus on safety, accountability, and communication on the overhaul line. “I tell the team, if something’s not safe or there’s a better way, speak up,” he said. “We’re going to address it, and we’re going to fix it.” Where generations meet The legacy feels most tangible when Yingling sees his sons working in the same facility where earlier generations built their careers. “When I walk through the shop and see them working, it makes me the proudest dad in the world,” he said. “It shows the railroad really does build something across generations.” For the Yingling family, the railroad has meant more than steady work. It has created opportunity , shaped values, and kept generations connected to their community. That continuity, from the earliest days of railroading in Altoona to today’s evolving technology and shop operations, reflects something deeper than tradition. It reflects a shared commitment to doing the work right, adapting as the industry advances, and passing that standard on to the next generation. Left: A handbrake wheel Dave restored to honor six generations of Yinglings. Right: Dave's grandson, Kynstin, at Altoona's Railroaders Memorial Museum. Roots and roles: Yingling family William J. Yingling, Carman (great-great-grandfather) Howard E.
